summary: Warmup traffic during scheduled scale-ups consumes tenant quota and triggers soft 429s for mixed realtime+batch workloads
description:
Issue summary: NovaSearch reports intermittent soft 429s impacting low-latency webchat sessions while a scheduled autoscaler scale-up runs concurrently with a nightly bulk embedding job. Impact: Several end users experienced additional latency and aborted requests during the scale-up window; customer reports 3-5% failed realtime requests during each scheduled ramp. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east, model pinned to gptx-11b-quant, autoscaler schedule runs 03:00-03:30 UTC nightly to add capacity for morning batch jobs. Observed behavior: During the scale-up window we see a steady cohort of short-lived 'warmup' client connections from the platform warmup service and the customer's prefetch workers. These short sessions create quota.debit entries and appear to be counted against the tenant's per-key concurrency/token buckets, causing temporary exhaustion for the customer's realtime route and manifesting as 429s with X-RateLimit-Reason: tenant_quota_exhausted (soft). Steps to reproduce: 1) Run a scheduled scale-up in a dedicated pool with 'prefetch' warmup enabled. 2) Start a small steady stream of concurrent low-latency chat sessions (10-50 concurrent). 3) Kick off a bulk embedding job that uses multiple ephemeral worker API keys. 4) Observe per-route and per-tenant quota counters in the 00-10 minute warmup window. Logs & evidence:
- quota.audit logs show repeated entries: "debit:tenant=novasearch,src=warmup-service,amt=1" correlated with scale-up start.
- API gateway metrics show increased short-lived connections (~200-400ms) from warmup workers.
- Error traces from customer's telemetry show 429s between timestamp 2026-03-10T03:05Z and 2026-03-10T03:17Z.
- Attached links (console traces): https://console.redwood.ai/trace/SUP-997531-warmup-trace (internal).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: warmup and prefetch traffic is not marked as 'quota-exempt' and is counted against tenant per-key buckets. We observed that the platform warmup service uses the same API key pool as the customer when running in dedicated mode and spawns many short sessions timed to complete model compilation/warm cache. Querying the quota accounting table shows bursts of small debits with source tag 'warmup-service' matching the scale-up lifecycle. We confirmed a spike in 'connection_open' events followed by immediate 'quota.debit' entries. Reproduced in staging by enabling scheduled scale-up and toggling 'prefetch=true' for worker service. Hypothesis validated: warmup worker calls decrement refill windows on per-key and per-tenant token buckets because warmup traffic flows through the same quota path as customer traffic. Engineering note: current quota pipeline assumes longer-lived sessions for amortization; short-lived warmup sessions create marginal accounting overhead per connection and can push tenants over concurrency window thresholds.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Samir Kapoor (customer): We see these 429s every night around the scheduled scale-up. Can Redwood exclude platform warmup traffic from our quota? This is blocking peak-hour users in the morning.
2026-03-10 11:05 - Support (Aisha Patel): Thanks Samir — investigating. We've pulled quota.audit slices and are confirming source tags. We're triaging with SRE and infra to reproduce in staging.

2026-03-10 13:20 - SRE (Jonas Müller): Reproduced in staging. Warmup worker spawns 120 short sessions at scale-up start; each session causes a per-key debit. Adding 'warmup' to source tags makes them identifiable but doesn't exempt accounting. Creating patch to add warmup_exempt flag into quota pipeline for dedicated pools.

2026-03-11 09:34 - Engineering (Marina Chen): Preliminary fix merged to feature branch: mark warmup sessions with header X-Warmup: true and gate quota debits for flagged sessions behind 'dedicated.warmup_exempt' config. Need rollout plan and safety checks for abuse prevention.

2026-03-12 15:10 - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer notified of hotfix timeline and temporary mitigations: 1) disable prefetch warmup on the NovaSearch side while we roll fix, 2) split realtime API key from bulk-ingest API key to isolate quotas, or 3) schedule scale-ups outside peak realtime windows. Customer responded they can disable prefetch for next two nights and will pilot key-split tomorrow.
workaround: Short-term: 1) Instruct NovaSearch to disable prefetch/warmup workers for the dedicated pool (config flag on their ingest workers). 2) Create separate API keys for realtime webchat vs bulk embedding workers to isolate per-key token buckets. 3) Move scheduled scale-up to a non-peak window if possible. These reduce burst accounting and restore realtime availability immediately.
resolution_plan: Hotfix: roll quota pipeline change to ignore debits from requests containing X-Warmup: true when the pool is configured with dedicated.warmup_exempt=true. Rollout steps: 1) Merge trunk PR and run canary in staging dedicated cluster. 2) Coordinate with SRE to enable dedicated.warmup_exempt for NovaSearch after verifying metrics. 3) Monitor for quota drift or abuse for 48 hours. Long-term: add console flag to show warmup traffic accounting and expose per-route quota separation templates for dedicated customers that mix realtime and bulk workloads.
follow_up_actions: Enable feature flag for NovaSearch and monitor quota usage for 48h post-rollout
Create KB article for customers titled 'Avoiding warmup-induced 429s during autoscaler events'
Add dashboard tile in Redwood Console showing warmup traffic as a distinct time series for dedicated pools
Postmortem if customer impact > 5% failed requests during rollouts
